text:
evan: Minimal repro: rollup + terser production bundle strips/renames our named export and users hit "TypeError: createClient is not a function" only in the minified prod build (dev works). Happens in browser and edge SSR builds.

evans: Repro steps:
1) fresh ts app with rollup config and rollup-plugin-terser
2) npm i @redwood/inference-sdk
3) import like: `import { createClient } from '@redwood/inference-sdk'` and call `createClient()`
4) rollup -c --environment NODE_ENV:production then serve bundle

evans: Prod console: `TypeError: (0 , sdk.createClient) is not a function`

mai: Can you paste the top of the built bundle where the sdk is inlined? In our repro we saw something like:
```js
// inlined chunk
var t = function(){/*...*/};
var n = {createClient: t};
exports.default = n; // or module.exports = n
```
Then the consumer side becomes `(0, sdk.createClient)` but after minify it's `(0, sdk.t)` and the shape differs after interop so the call fails.

evans: Yep exactly. In a different build the package got resolved to the CJS wrapper and rollup/terser ended up renaming the inner function while webpack dev server kept the ESM shape so dev worked.

oscar: Two immediate axes to fix: package publish (longer-term) and bundler config (short-term). On package: provide a clear `exports` map with `import`/`browser` keys that point to a pure-ESM bundle that uses real named exports, avoid shipping top-level CJS wrapper files that do `module.exports = require('./cjs')`. Also ensure `types` exists at root and consider `typesVersions` for TS pathing.

zara: On bundler side, we reproduced the issue and a stopgap that worked was disabling top-level toplevel name mangling in terser. rollup-plugin-terser config we used:
```js
terser({
  mangle: { toplevel: false },
  keep_fnames: true
})
```
That preserved exported function names and the error disappeared. Not ideal for long-term but useful for CI smoke tests.

mai: Another short-term workaround for consumers: import default and call `sdk.createClient()` instead of named import. Ugly for DX but quick. Also pin rollup `preserveEntrySignatures: 'strict'` sometimes helps.

oscar: We'll cut a canary that: (1) adds an `exports` map with \"import\" and \"browser\" -> dist/esm, (2) adds `type: \"module\"` for the ESM bundle, (3) ensures dist/esm/index.js uses `export function createClient(){}` named export (no re-export wrappers), and (4) publishes `dist/types/index.d.ts` and sets root `types`.

ci-bot: Ticket DEVEX-954 created: publish canary + add prod-bundle smoke test (rollup/webpack/vite) to CI.

evans: I'll pin a CI job in sample-app to run rollup production build with terser and fail on runtime errors so we catch this early.

zara: Quick note for docs: add a small section "Prod minify & named export gotchas" with tips: prefer clean exports map, avoid CJS wrappers, add root types, and if necessary adjust terser mangle/keep_fnames for the prod build.

oscar: publishing canary now, will post canary tag and link to PR.

evans: thanks all — saved my Friday. :tada:
